answer_summary: With L = neutral tetradentate ligand 8: 9 is cis-[FeII(L)(H2O)2]2+ (OS 2, CN 6, VE 18, Z 2); 10 is [FeI(L)(H2O)]+ (1,5,17,1); 11 is [FeIII(L)(kappa2-C,O-CO2)] + with formal CO2(2-) (3,6,17,1); 12 is C-bound [FeII(L)(COOH)]+ (2,5,16,1); 13 is [FeII(L)(COOH)(H2O)]+ (2,6,18,1); 14 is [FeII(L)(CO)(H2O)]2+ (2,6,18,2); and 15 is [FeII(L)(H2O)]2+ (2,5,16,2).
assumptions: Ligand 8 is represented exactly at the neutral tetradentate N4-cartoon resolution mandated by Q8.4; its noncoordinating carboxylic acid substituent remains neutral as drawn on Q8-1.
The printed arrow labels obey conservation of total charge, with electron charge -1, proton charge +1, chloride charge -1, and H2O, CO2, and CO neutral.
Oxidation states and valence-electron counts use standard ionic organometallic bookkeeping: Fe is group 8 and each bound donor atom supplies two electrons.
Absolute octahedral axis names in Lean are arbitrary labels; only the chemically relevant cis relation of the two labile sites is asserted.
